# ClassConstantUsageCorrectness

<Badge type="danger" text="error" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" /> 

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs) · PhpStorm name: `ClassConstantUsageCorrectnessInspection`

`Foo::class` is resolved at compile time from the name *as written*, so a
class name typed with the wrong letter case (or imported with the wrong case)
produces a string that differs from the real class name. That string then
breaks case-sensitive comparisons, array keys, container ids and autoloaders
on case-sensitive file systems.

## Example

```php{13,14,16,28,43,44}
<?php

namespace Catalog {
    class Product {}
    class Variant {}
}

namespace Storefront {
    use Catalog\product;
    use Catalog\Variant as Option;

    return [
        Product::class,
        OPTION::class,
        Option::class,
        Widgets\banner::class,
        Widgets\Banner::class,
    ];
}

namespace Storefront\Widgets {
    use Catalog\Product;

    class Banner {}

    return [
        Product::class,
        product::class,
        banner::class,
    ];
}

namespace Checkout {
    use Storefront\Widgets as W;
    use Storefront\Widgets\Banner as Promo;

    class Cart
    {
        public function names()
        {
            return [
                W\Banner::class,
                W\BANNER::class,
                \arrayobject::class,
                \ArrayObject::class,
                Promo::class,
                self::class,
                static::class,
            ];
        }
    }
}
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 13: Letter case of the class name differs from its declaration; ::class will return the wrong string.</li>
<li>line 14: Letter case of the class name differs from its declaration; ::class will return the wrong string.</li>
<li>line 16: Letter case of the class name differs from its declaration; ::class will return the wrong string.</li>
<li>line 28: Letter case of the class name differs from its declaration; ::class will return the wrong string.</li>
<li>line 43: Letter case of the class name differs from its declaration; ::class will return the wrong string.</li>
<li>line 44: Letter case of the class name differs from its declaration; ::class will return the wrong string.</li>
</ul>

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "ClassConstantUsageCorrectness": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file), either of:

```php
// @custos-ignore ClassConstantUsageCorrectness

/**
 * @noinspection ClassConstantUsageCorrectnessInspection
 */
```
